holidays.name: International Archives Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the dusty, unsung heroes of history: archives, archivists, and the mountains of old paperwork that keep humanity's memory from falling apart. Think of it as a love letter to filing cabinets everywhere.
holidays.origin: Established by the International Council on Archives (ICA), which was founded on June 9, 1948, under UNESCO's auspices. The day was formally recognized by the ICA in 2007 to raise awareness of the importance of preserving records.
holidays.funFact: The ICA's founding on June 9 is the reason for the date, and archives around the world hold everything from ancient clay tablets to modern emails, making them the original cloud storage.

holidays.name: Donald Duck Day
holidays.description: A quacking good celebration of Disney's famously short-tempered, sailor-suit-wearing, pants-averse duck. Fans binge cartoons, practice their best garbled Donald voice, and try not to lose their tempers.
holidays.origin: Donald Duck made his debut in the Disney cartoon 'The Wise Little Hen' on June 9, 1934, and fans have marked the date as his unofficial birthday ever since.
holidays.funFact: Donald's voice actor, Clarence 'Ducky' Nash, originally auditioned with a goat-voice recitation of 'Mary Had a Little Lamb,' and Walt Disney was so impressed he created the duck around that voice.

holidays.name: Strawberry Rhubarb Pie Day
holidays.description: A tart-meets-sweet celebration of the pie that proves fruit and vegetable can live in harmony. Rhubarb is technically a vegetable, but it's usually too sour to eat alone, so it gets a sugary strawberry bodyguard.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday popularized by pie lovers and food calendars, timed to early summer when both strawberries and rhubarb are in season in many parts of the United States.
holidays.funFact: In 1947, a U.S. customs court in Buffalo, New York ruled rhubarb legally a fruit to lower import taxes, since fruits were taxed less than vegetables.

holidays.name: Superman Day
holidays.description: Fans around the world put on capes, strike heroic poses, and remember that sometimes the best disguise is just a pair of glasses. A salute to the Man of Steel and his questionable ability to fool coworkers.
holidays.origin: Observed in the comic-fan community to honor the Man of Steel, who made his debut in Action Comics #1 in 1938.
holidays.funFact: Superman originally could not fly. In his earliest comics he could only leap over tall buildings in a single bound, and the flying power came later.

holidays.name: Cheese Day (Cheese Fest Celebration)
holidays.description: A cheesy tribute to all things dairy. Cheese enthusiasts sample wedges, wheels, and curds, and debate whether the stinkier the cheese, the better.
holidays.origin: An informal celebration among cheese lovers that has spread through social media and food calendars, giving people one more excuse to build a cheese board.
holidays.funFact: The United States makes more cheese than any other country in the world, and an average American eats around 40 pounds of it every year.
